title: The whole machine
note: v5 (31 Oct, Rajat's 4th review): plays after section 8 and before section 9. text = subtitles; say = spelled for the voice. Numbers from brain3d/trace.json, films/qkv_data.json, build/data/structure_data.json and build/data/finale_data.json.

blocks.text: Here is the whole machine, from start to finish, on one question. Emma asks: how many city e-bike battery packs do we have in Manchester stores?
blocks.say: Here is the whole machine, from start to finish, on one question. Emma asks: how many city e-bike battery packs do we have in Manchester stores?

blocks.text: The app wraps her words in a chat: its own instructions, her question, and a header that says the assistant speaks next. The tokenizer cuts all of it into 100 tiles, each with its own number. The date is cut digit by digit. Manchester is a single tile, number 19361.
blocks.say: The app wraps her words in a chat: its own instructions, her question, and a header that says the assistant speaks next. The tokenizer cuts all of it into one hundred tiles, each with its own number. The date is cut digit by digit. Manchester is a single tile, number one nine three six one.

blocks.text: Each tile looks up its row in the embedding table. The table has 151,936 rows, one for every token the model knows. Each row is 896 numbers. So every tile now stands with a column of 896 numbers behind it.
blocks.say: Each tile looks up its row in the embedding table. The table has one hundred and fifty-one thousand, nine hundred and thirty-six rows, one for every token the model knows. Each row is eight hundred and ninety-six numbers. So every tile now stands with a column of eight hundred and ninety-six numbers behind it.

blocks.text: The 100 columns enter block 1. First, attention. Each position makes a query, a key and a value. Its query meets the keys of the earlier positions, never the later ones, and the values of the best matches flow in. Then the MLP reworks each column on its own.
blocks.say: The hundred columns enter block one. First, attention. Each position makes a query, a key and a value. Its query meets the keys of the earlier positions, never the later ones, and the values of the best matches flow in. Then the MLP reworks each column on its own.

blocks.text: Attention is not one look, but fourteen, side by side: the heads. Each head looks in its own way. In block 24, head 2 puts 65 percent of its weight on Manchester. In block 12, head 13 rests all of its weight on the very first token.
blocks.say: Attention is not one look, but fourteen, side by side: the heads. Each head looks in its own way. In block twenty-four, head two puts sixty-five percent of its weight on Manchester. In block twelve, head thirteen rests all of its weight on the very first token.

blocks.text: Every block updates all 100 columns, not just the last one, all the way through 24 blocks. The other columns matter: at every block, they hold the keys and values the last column reads. The stack holds 494,032,768 learnt numbers, every one set in training, as we saw in section 8.
blocks.say: Every block updates all one hundred columns, not just the last one, all the way through twenty-four blocks. The other columns matter: at every block, they hold the keys and values the last column reads. The stack holds four hundred and ninety-four million, thirty-two thousand, seven hundred and sixty-eight learnt numbers, every one set in training, as we saw in section eight.

blocks.text: At the top, only the last column speaks. It is scored against every row of the same table, all 151,936. Softmax turns the scores into probabilities. We: 56 percent. As: 8. Manchester: 6. We is chosen.
blocks.say: At the top, only the last column speaks. It is scored against every row of the same table, all one hundred and fifty-one thousand, nine hundred and thirty-six. Softmax turns the scores into probabilities. We: fifty-six percent. As: eight. Manchester: six. We is chosen.

blocks.text: We joins the row, and the machine runs again. But the 100 earlier columns are not run again. Their keys and values were kept, in the KV cache. So each new token sends just one new column through the 24 blocks, and that column still reads every position before it. Currently. Have. A space.
blocks.say: We joins the row, and the machine runs again. But the hundred earlier columns are not run again. Their keys and values were kept, in the K V cache. So each new token sends just one new column through the twenty-four blocks, and that column still reads every position before it. Currently. Have. A space.

blocks.text: Then the number. One, at 34 percent. Zero. Zero. Token by token, the answer grows: We currently have 100 city e-bike battery packs available in our Manchester stores. Then the end-of-turn token, and the loop stops.
blocks.say: Then the number. One, at thirty-four percent. Zero. Zero. Token by token, the answer grows: We currently have one hundred city e-bike battery packs available in our Manchester stores. Then the end-of-turn token, and the loop stops.

blocks.text: Every step ran exactly as it was built to. Nothing broke. And still, the answer is 100. Ledgerline, Northbridge's own record, says 5,400. So why did a machine that worked perfectly make this number up?
blocks.say: Every step ran exactly as it was built to. Nothing broke. And still, the answer is one hundred. Ledgerline, Northbridge's own record, says five thousand four hundred. So why did a machine that worked perfectly make this number up?
